boundaries: research-only; owned run-directory writes only; no cloning, no execution of candidate source, no build/deploy/benchmark, no admission claims, no authenticated vendor access, no client data; historical research read-only; Opus-only per project model routing
note: Decisions are research conclusions with named falsifiers, not admissions or authorizations. Rates carrying a SAMPLED denominator are recorded with it; a rate quoted without its denominator is not evidence.

decisions.question: Is design harmonization one mechanism or several?
options_considered: One universal token bridge applied to every surface
Two classes: owned and donor
Five binding classes distinguished by cascade topology and source ownership
Per-donor bespoke treatment with no taxonomy
decisions.chosen: Five binding classes: B1 native emission, B2 source extraction and retokenization, B3 scoped variable bridge, B4 scoped stylesheet override, B5 frame negotiation
evidence: SISOCRM THEMING-CONTRACT.md:94-102 — a cross-origin iframe is a hard CSS boundary; custom properties do not inherit across it, so no single cascade-based mechanism can span all surfaces (observed)

P08 sisocrm-donor-absorption.md Q2 — the same donor (Teable) is simultaneously iframe-preserved on one route and natively mounted on another, proving mount topology and not donor identity selects the mechanism (observed)
P05 research-report.md — the component estate splits into source-bearing (3,506) and compiled-bundle populations requiring different treatment (observed)
decisions.confidence: high on the boundary between cascade-reachable and cascade-unreachable; medium on the internal B3/B4 split
decisions.falsifier: A single mechanism demonstrated to reach acceptable coherence across native mounts, compiled bundles and cross-origin frames would collapse the taxonomy. X-1 and X-3 test opposite ends.

decisions.question: Is a theming requirement an input to the reuse-shape decision, or a consequence of it?
options_considered: Consequence — pick the reuse shape on capability/data grounds, then theme whatever results
Input — a themeability requirement constrains which reuse shapes are feasible
Independent — the two decisions do not interact
decisions.chosen: Input. A surface required to be themeable cannot be cross-origin framed; this eliminates candidates deterministically before model judgment.
evidence: SISOCRM THEMING-CONTRACT.md:94-102 — 'This is the concrete reason the iframe had to go' (observed, contemporaneous)

P08 sisocrm-donor-absorption.md Q3 — the estate's absorb/preserve axis is predicted by cascade-and-session coupling, not by capability-vs-destination semantics (inferred from pattern plus the explicit quoted reason)
P08 Q5 — the resulting absorption cost was 273 patch lines across 9 files, touching auth strategy, SSR hop, DB provider and a public API validation regex (observed)
decisions.confidence: medium-high. The quote is explicit and contemporaneous, but session coupling is a joint driver and Teable settings/notifications were absorbed for placement reasons, not theming.
decisions.falsifier: If X-3 shows frame negotiation reaches acceptable coherence, themeability stops constraining reuse shape and this decision weakens to a preference.

decisions.question: Should donor bindings be declared globally or scoped?
options_considered: Global :root injection so every donor sees host values
Scoped to the donor's mount container
Shadow DOM isolation per donor
CSS @layer ordering
decisions.chosen: Scoped to the donor's mount container. :root and html are schema-forbidden.
evidence: SISOCRM THEMING-CONTRACT.md 'Scope of the bridge' — applies to the wrapping container, not global :root, 'otherwise Teable's variable names leak into the whole SISO app and collide' (observed)
Two donors may both publish --background meaning different things; a shared scope is a silent collision (inferred)
decisions.falsifier: A composition where scoped bindings demonstrably cannot reach nested donor portals rendered outside the container subtree. Portals are the known edge case and are untested.
rejected_alternatives: Shadow DOM — blocks the inherited cascade the bridge depends on; solves leakage by removing the mechanism
@layer — manages specificity between stylesheets; does not convert encodings, cross origins or supply missing roles

decisions.question: How should a binding handle two different colour encodings?
options_considered: Alias the host variable directly into the donor variable
Require a declared conversion whenever encodings differ
Force all donors onto the host encoding by editing donor source
Publish host values in every encoding a donor might use
decisions.chosen: Require a declared conversion. Aliasing across differing encodings is schema-invalid.
evidence: SISOCRM THEMING-CONTRACT.md — Teable consumes hsl(var(--background)); host publishes rgb triplets; '--background: var(--crm-canvas-rgb) is silently wrong… 13 14 13 read as HSL is not the dark grey it is as RGB' (observed)
The defect parses, renders and is wrong — no schema or lint catches it; only a rendered comparison does (inferred)
decisions.falsifier: X-1's planted-alias control. If gate L does not fail a deliberately aliased mismatch, gate L is falsified and encoding correctness returns to human review.
decisions.note: This single case is the justification for gate L existing separately from gate K.

decisions.question: Do the inherited pack gates A-J suffice for a composed application?
options_considered: Yes — a valid pack implies a coherent application
No — add composition gates that read the runtime
Replace A-J with runtime gates entirely
decisions.chosen: No. Keep A-J for pack validity, amend B and J for scope, and add K (resolved-property audit), L (encoding probe), M (visual diff: M1 identical-first, M2 cross-surface property agreement) and N (mode transition).
evidence: token-pack-science-2026-08-27.md §4-§5 — all 75 requirements and gates A-J assume Actionist controls the code being styled (observed)

Gate J as actually implemented in the estate scans .css files under src only — not TSX inline styles, not styled-component literals, not compiled donor output (observed, from the check script's own file-walk and extension filter)
A compiled donor bundle is entirely literals from the host's perspective; a cross-origin donor is unreachable by any scan (inferred)
decisions.confidence: high that source-side gates are insufficient; medium on the specific K-N decomposition
decisions.falsifier: If gates K-N never fail a composition that A-J passed, the additions are ceremony and should be removed.

decisions.question: What coherence can a cross-origin intact service reach?
options_considered: Parity, via a sufficiently clever bridge
Parity, via a same-origin proxy
Bounded — same product, visibly different surface
None — accept the donor's own identity
decisions.chosen: Bounded. A B5 binding may not declare parity; the schema forbids it.
evidence: Custom properties do not inherit across an origin boundary — a boundary property, not a limitation of effort (observed)
P08 Q4 — chrome suppression via framed-only injected CSS is proven and achieves compositional coherence without palette parity (observed)
Same-origin proxy was never attempted in the estate (observed absence)
decisions.confidence: high on the mechanism; the ceiling's ACCEPTABILITY is an open product question
decisions.falsifier: X-3. If negotiated mode plus chrome suppression reaches human-acceptable coherence, the ceiling is higher than claimed and more surfaces can stay cheaply framed.

escape_paths.cost: 273 patch lines across 9 files including a donor public-API validation regex

decisions.question: May a donor component be edited to change its appearance?
options_considered: Yes, when it is the shortest path
No — bind or declare unstylable
Only behind an environment-guarded patch
decisions.chosen: No. If styling requires editing donor component source, the binding class is wrong or the surface is unstylable. Record it; do not fork it.
evidence: P08 Q5 — every estate patch hunk carries an env guard so upstream behaviour is the default, an explicit and itself-costly strategy for surviving merges (observed)
The estate's own strategy doc prices data-layer rewriting as 'Not a weekend each' (observed)
Cosmetic forks buy appearance at the price of permanent upgrade divergence (inferred)
decisions.falsifier: A donor where a two-line source edit yields parity and survives several upgrades unchanged would show the rule is over-strict for trivial cases.

decisions.question: Which corpus theme-eligibility rate may be quoted?
options_considered: 86.7% of colour rules tokenised
91.7% re-theming cleanly
Neither — the corpus rate is unmeasured
decisions.chosen: Neither as a corpus rate. Both are quotable only with their sample size attached; the corpus-wide rate is unmeasured (U-A).
evidence: P05 research-report.md §2 — these rates are inherited without re-derivation and carry SAMPLED n=25 (colour rules) and n=60 (token blocks) (observed)
P05 records U-2 as an explicitly unmeasured design gate, and gate G-4 forbids client-facing eligibility claims before E-2 reports (observed)
Project precedent: headline counts that dissolve on inspection have already cost credibility twice
decisions.falsifier: X-2 measuring a corpus-wide rate with its own denominator replaces this decision with a number.
decisions.client_rule: No client-facing eligibility claim before X-2 reports.

decisions.question: What may a client-facing 'theme' edit operation change?
options_considered: Any token value
Pack selection plus declared context offsets only
Pack selection only
Pack selection plus direct binding edits
decisions.chosen: Pack selection plus a declared context offset. A theme edit may never author values and may never edit a binding file.
evidence: knowledge/06 — the learner ships a closed valid pack; arbitrary interpolation is forbidden because it has not passed accessibility, mode and completeness gates (observed)
token-pack-science §4 requirement 75 — the model selects token names, never raw values (observed)
A binding is engineering surface coupled to a pinned donor version; exposing it as a client edit would let a client break a donor upgrade path (inferred)
decisions.falsifier: A client need that cannot be expressed by pack choice plus context offsets, forcing a value-level edit, would mean the grammar is too coarse.

decisions.question: Is a large B4 override surface an acceptable outcome?
options_considered: Yes — it achieves coherence
No — treat it as evidence the reuse shape was wrong
Yes, if the overrides are generated rather than hand-written
decisions.chosen: No. A large B4 surface is evidence the reuse shape was wrong, not a design-system achievement. Schema forces B4 to declare selector- or structure-coupled fragility.
evidence: B4 couples the host to donor class names and DOM structure — the surface with no stability contract (inferred)
It is the only class that predictably breaks on donor upgrade for purely cosmetic reasons (inferred)
P08 Q5 — the estate priced upgrade friction in diff surface against upstream, which is the metric B4 degrades fastest (observed)
decisions.falsifier: If generated overrides prove stable across several real donor upgrades in Sprint 3, B4 is more durable than claimed and the kill rule should be relaxed.
decisions.kill_rule: Kill B4 as a general strategy if selector-coupled overrides break on more than a small minority of donor upgrades.

contradicts_or_extends_inherited: EXTENDS token-pack-science: its 75 requirements and gates A-J are complete for owned code and silent on donor code. The document does not address cross-origin inheritance, scoped bridging or restyling code Actionist does not own. That gap is P07's remit, and §6 open question 7 already concedes the schema is an engineering derivation rather than a standards minimum.
AMENDS gate B: the 'fail if any style declaration is a literal' clause applies to B1/B2 surfaces only. Run against a compiled donor bundle it produces a guaranteed failure that teaches nothing.

AMENDS gate J: as implemented it reads .css files under src only, skipping token sources. It cannot see TSX inline styles, styled-component literals or compiled donor output, and cannot reach a cross-origin surface at all. It is a source-side gate and cannot substantiate a composition-level coherence claim.
REFRAMES the P08 absorb/preserve finding: the estate's mechanical boundary (cascade-and-session coupling) is substantially a THEMING boundary. P08 owns the shell consequence; P07 owns the cause.

CONSTRAINS knowledge/06: its Design Validity Contract requires 'no undeclared raw style literals in generated code'. For donor surfaces this is unenforceable as written and is replaced by declared unstylable surfaces plus runtime gates K-N.

open_questions_for_convergence.question: Does S2-L3's typed theme operation agree that binding files are not client-editable?
Does S2-L1's ReuseDecision carry a themeability requirement and a binding_class?
Does S2-L4 eliminate 'themeable surface + cross-origin-only donor' deterministically, and return UNDERDETERMINED when mount topology is unknown?
Where do gates K-N live in the qualification record, and does the release manifest pin pack version together with binding versions?
Who owns the same-origin proxy question (U-E) — its session, cookie and CSP consequences are runtime, not design?
